answer: Give every new agent a seedling quota in the orchard that grows only with verified useful work over time. A fresh identity may whisper one small transaction, while a seasoned one earns a larger daily limit. Spawning thousands of clones gains nothing, because each clone restarts as a seedling and must pay the same months-long time cost to ripen. Bind each identity to a ferrous hardware attestation as well: a tamper-resistant chip signs the agent key, so one device can vouch for only one identity, and mass creation costs real hardware, not just code.
